title: Runtime Sandboxing Experiment Lab Manual (2025)
body:
> **Archived 2026-01-12:** this page is superseded by "Runtime Sandboxing Experiment Lab Manual" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

This manual covers the lab sandbox the runtime team uses for invasive performance experiments, kernel-scheduler patches, and mixed-workload benchmarks, kept away from production. It describes the architecture, isolation model, experiment runbook, profiling and telemetry expectations, benchmark invocation, known issues, and lab incident runbooks.

Goals

- Reproducible, auditable environment for risky runtime changes.
- Full isolation from production control planes; no telemetry or credential leakage.
- A common profiling and benchmarking workflow so runs are comparable.
- Documented failure modes and mitigations.

Audience

- Runtime engineers working on kernels and schedulers.
- Performance engineers running comparative benchmarks.
- SREs supporting lab infrastructure.

High-level sandbox architecture

Components

- lab-gateway: ingress that routes experiment traffic and enforces quotas.
- kernel-orchestrator: deploys custom kernels/kernelspecs to lab nodes.
- sandbox-runner: per-node agent for cgroups, MIG partitions, GPU modes, and kernel module overrides.
- kvcache-sim: synthetic KV cache emulating prefix/session caching.
- telemetry-proxy: stamps lab telemetry with lab_run_id and writes it to the lab telemetry bucket.

Isolation model

- Network: lab runs are confined to the lab VPC (vpc-lab-1) with no peering to prod. Egress goes through nat-lab using explicit allow lists.
- Compute: nodes carry the label "lab:true" in a dedicated autoscaling group; images ship the debug kernel and a signed kernel module whitelist.
- GPU: NVIDIA MPS per experiment (multi-process concurrency) or MIG partitions (perf isolation), toggled by sandbox-runner.
- Storage and secrets: ephemeral PVCs; secrets come from the lab KMS with a short TTL and never replicate to production KMS.

Kernel-scheduling considerations

- Scheduler builds available via kernel-orchestrator: baseline, preemptive-slice, and adaptive-slice, each tagged with a driver/CUDA compatibility matrix.
- Priority mapping: map Redwood priority classes to kernel priorities in the experiment config, e.g. "interactive" -> SCHED_RR with 5ms quantum; "batch" -> SCHED_DEADLINE with ED=50ms/1s.
- Fairness accounting: for cooperative preemption tests, set enable_credit_accounting=true to observe queue-smear.

Experiment environment provisioning

1) Request sandbox allocation

- File an RFC in the experiments tracker with title, hypothesis, node types, GPU mode, expected run time, and roll-back criteria.
- After approval: ./scripts/request-lab --project runtime --nodes 4 --gputype a100 --duration 8h --labels preemptive-test

2) Provisioning checklist

- Nodes in the ASG are labeled lab:true.
- kernel-orchestrator has deployed the requested kernel tag.
- GPU mode applied: kubectl get nodes -l lab=true -o json | jq '.items[].metadata.annotations.gpu_mode'
- telemetry-proxy has the lab_run_id and bucket path.

Step-by-step experiment runbook

1. Prepare experiment config (experiment-config.yaml):

experiment_name: preemptive-slice-compare-2025
environment: staging-sim
node_selectors:
  - lab:true
kernel_tag: preemptive-slice-v2
gpu_mode: MIG-1g.5gb
workload_profiles:
  - name: interactive
    qps: 120
    seq_length_p95: 320
  - name: batch
    qps: 2
    seq_length_p95: 2048
measurement_windows_s: 300
telemetry_bucket: s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2025/experiment-123

2. Smoke run (5 min)

- Check functional correctness, service health, and telemetry tags.
- ./lab-runner start --config experiment-config.yaml --smoke

3. Full run

- ./lab-runner start --config experiment-config.yaml --duration 3600 --trace-sampling 0.1
- Monitor with kubectl top nodes -l lab=true and ./observability/quick-check --run-id=experiment-123

4. Collect artifacts

- Kernel traces: /var/log/lab/experiments/experiment-123/kernel-trace.tar.gz
- Flamegraphs: s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2025/experiment-123/flamegraphs/
- Perf counters: s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2025/experiment-123/perf/
- Manifest: s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2025/experiment-123/manifest.json

Profiling playbook (lab-specific)

- Sampling: 10% probabilistic sampling for p50/p95, 100% for p99+ traces during the first 5 minutes, then 1% for the rest of the run.
- Metrics: wall_time, kernel_queue_time, kv_cache_hit, gpu_busy_time, gpu_memory_alloc, context_switches/sec, scheduler_runqueue_length.
- Tracing: runtime-gateway and kernel-orchestrator must put lab_run_id and experiment_name on root spans.
- Perf tooling: perf + Nsight CLI on A100, e.g. sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 300; perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl > flame.svg

Benchmarking suite invocation

- ./bench-suite/run --profile latency --shards 4 --concurrency 64 --model redwood-v0.9-quant --seed 42 --out s3://lab-telemetry/runtime/2025/experiment-123/bench

config_key,description,default,lab_override
shards,number of client shards,4,4
concurrency,total outstanding requests per shard,32,64
sequence_distribution,which lengths to sample,prod-like,tail-enhanced
model_variant,model binary to run,baseline,preemptive-slice-v2

Data hygiene and retention

- Lab telemetry is tagged with lab_run_id and kept with a retention of 30 days by default. Sensitive experiments get confidentiality 'restricted' and a security contact.
- Never import lab telemetry into production dashboards; share aggregated metrics only.

Known issues and mitigations

- Driver mismatch causing node panic: pin the driver to the node image and verify with ./scripts/verify-driver.sh; cordon and reprovision on mismatch.
- telemetry-proxy dropping spans at >2k RPS: lower trace sampling or scale telemetry-proxy (HPA target cpu 70%).
- kvcache-sim TTL inconsistencies under load: raise kvcache-sim replica_count to at least 2 and enable read-through logging.

Incident runbooks for lab activities

1) Node panic during experiment

- Pause: ./lab-runner pause --run-id=experiment-123
- Cordon: kubectl cordon <node-id> && kubectl describe node <node-id> | tee /tmp/node-diagnostics.txt
- Kernel oops: sudo journalctl -k -b -1 > /tmp/kernel-oops.txt and attach to the incident.
- Reprovision: ./scripts/reprovision-node --node <node-id> --ami ami-lab-debug-20251001

2) Telemetry corruption

- Check manifest: aws s3 cp s3://lab-telemetry/.../manifest.json - | jq .status
- Missing files: escalate to telemetry-eng@redwood.com and mark the run partial.

Safety and approvals

- Experiments that change kernel scheduling semantics with possible tenant-isolation impact need security review and SRE sign-off via the experiment-approval workflow.

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: runtime-experiments@redwood.com (Runtime Performance)
- Lab infra on-call: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Telemetry owner: telemetry-eng@redwood.com

Appendix: quick reference commands

- ./scripts/request-lab --nodes 4 --duration 8h
- ./bench-suite/run --profile latency --out <s3path>
- ./lab-runner start --config experiment-config.yaml --smoke
- sudo tar czf /var/log/lab/experiments/<run>/kernel-trace.tar.gz /sys/kernel/debug/tracing

Document history

- Written by Maya Alvarez (runtime-experiments); contributors Arjun Patel and Sofia Lin. This edition is no longer maintained; refer to the current lab manual.
